gaps.sentence: Mount Everest, ___ was first climbed in 1953, attracts hundreds of climbers every year.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' introduces extra information about the mountain; 'that' is wrong after a comma.

gaps.sentence: She was two hours late, ___ annoyed the interviewer.
gaps.hint: comment on the whole situation before the comma
gaps.explanation: When a clause comments on the whole previous statement, use 'which' after the comma.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: The 1990s was the decade ___ mobile phones became common.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'in which' after time nouns; 'which' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: The author, about ___ there has been much debate, will speak at the festival.
gaps.hint: debate about the author — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: 'About whom' is required after the preposition 'about' when referring to a person.

gaps.sentence: Pablo, ___ speaks five languages, works as an interpreter.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clauses about people take 'who'; 'that' never follows a comma in standard English.

gaps.sentence: The woman ___ won the prize gave a short speech.
gaps.explanation: The gap is the subject pronoun for a person, so 'who' is needed; 'whose' would show possession.

gaps.sentence: The director, ___ we met at the conference, has written to us.
gaps.hint: person as object, but the clause is non-defining
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses 'that' cannot replace 'who', even when the person is the object.
